players.product: KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) anti-PD-1 therapy; intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157), jointly developed with Moderna

quarterly_data.signal: Merck's Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K): the FDA approved KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX, each with Trodelvy, for first-line treatment of PD-L1 positive (CPS 10 or more) advanced triple-negative breast cancer (KEYNOTE-D19/ASCENT-04); the FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation to calderasib (MK-1084), an investigational oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, with KEYTRUDA for first-line KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC expressing PD-L1 (TPS 1% or more); the FDA approved an additional indication for CAPVAXIVE in children and adolescents aged 2 through 17 at increased risk for pneumococcal disease (Phase 3 STRIDE-13); KEYTRUDA as monotherapy significantly improved PFS versus chemotherapy in certain patients with advanced or recurrent mismatch-repair-deficient endometrial cancer (Phase 3 KEYNOTE-C93); ENFLONSIA received regulatory approvals in Japan and China for preventing RSV lower respiratory tract disease in infants; the European Commission approved KEYTRUDA plus Padcev for adults with cisplatin-ineligible resectable muscle-invasive bladder cancer; and the animal health business completed the acquisition of TARGAN, broadening its commercial poultry portfolio. China pharmaceutical sales were $368 million in Q2 2026 (Q2 2025: $407 million). The raised 2026 sales outlook of $66.3 billion to $67.3 billion compares with prior guidance of $65.8 billion to $67.0 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: prior 2026 sales guidance $65.8 billion to $67.0 billion; China Q2 2026 sales $368 million
